crime_highlights: witnessed the appellant place what appeared to be a black handgun on his dashboard
The passenger promptly turned back and called 911.
police seized a sawed off .22 calibre rifle and a black Airsoft BB gun that had been deposited nearby
It was the Airsoft the appellant had displayed earlier by the side of the road.
rationale_highlights: The three reports—the PSR, the original IRCA and the updated IRCA—all reflect the deprivations experienced by the appellant, a racialized young man.
The gravity of the appellant’s offence and his moral culpability for it must be assessed in the context of historic factors and systemic racism.

take into account the impact that social and economic deprivation, historical disadvantage, diminished and non-existent opportunities, and restricted options may have had on the offender’s moral responsibility
note: No victim harm; offence is displaying an Airsoft gun and possessing a sawed-off rifle.

crime_highlights: N.K. became pregnant as a result of sexual intercourse with R.B.W.
In the ninth month of her pregnancy, her mother threw her out of the house.
The baby was born with serious medical complications and significant developmental delays.
N.K.’s intellectual disabilities deprived her of the ability to care for the baby who was placed into permanent care with foster parents.
rationale_highlights: systemic and background factors may bear on the culpability of the offender, to the extent that they shed light on his or her level of moral blameworthiness
The constrained circumstances of African Nova Scotian offenders may diminish moral culpability
He has been impacted by historical deprivation, social and economic deprivation, as well as diminished and virtually non-existent opportunities.

Unfortunately, [R.B.W.] was not only a victim of historical impacts of racism, but as a consequence he fell into the control of the State and was abused physically, emotionally, and sexually by persons in positions of authority.
The information in the report informs the principles of sentencing and the weight that I should accord to denunciation and general deterrence.
exposed his vulnerabilities and impact[ed] his level of moral blameworthiness
note: Majority upholds the trial judge's reasoning, quoted in paras 107 and 112.

crime_highlights: she had severe injuries to the left side of her face
Her left face, left eye and lips were swollen and covered in blood.
it was her boyfriend, Harry Cope (the Appellant), who had assaulted her
The assault was captured on video and witnessed by passers-by.
rationale_highlights: In the appellant’s case his circumstances included a severe mental illness, significant drug addiction, a lack of culturally-focused treatment and support, and the overarching Gladue factors, all of which, in combination, impacted his moral culpability and the proportionality calculus.
the presence of addiction or mental health problems in an Indigenous individual must be viewed through the lens of the residual effects of residential schools and intergenerational trauma
the residential school experience is a factor in the appellant’s immediate family
This too is relevant to assessing the appellant’s moral blameworthiness and why it has been challenging for him to manage his addictions and mental illness.
note: Crime passage includes agreed facts; victim named in source but not highlighted.
